records.two_predicates_ruling: The two schedule counts the estate publishes are produced by DIFFERENT TESTS and are not guaranteed to agree: /v1/hypervisor/operations admits `schedule_spec.is_object()` and never reads `enabled`, while the loop admits `enabled == true && schedule_is_active(spec)`. Consequently NO estate record marks a run as scheduler-dispatched — the work-ledger run entries for the 09:00 cron slots carry trigger_kind: manual like every other run. The surface therefore answers WHEN a schedule will fire and REFUSES to answer WHICH PAST RUNS WERE FIRES: a time-correlation between a run timestamp and a cron slot would be this surface inventing an edge no record holds. self_report_scope_finding.ruling: no count on the surface is taken from a stage's own status field. unwritten_key_finding.claim: A SELECTION THE ROUTE ACCEPTS IS STILL A GAP WHEN THE KEY IT FILTERS ON IS NEVER WRITTEN BY THE RECORDS IT IS MEANT TO SCOPE.
unwritten_key_finding.the_easy_wrong_conclusion: GET /v1/hypervisor/work-ledger accepts ?project=…, applies it server-side, and returns a correctly filtered result. It is published on the daemon's own index, it needs no credential at this posture, and it reaches records that name a model. Every surface-level test for 'can this chooser be wired' says yes — including the one MS-1 taught, since here the parameter the form collects IS a parameter the route enforces. Wiring it would have produced a chooser that works in review and lies in production.
instances: THE FILTER'S KEY IS NOT ON THE ROWS IT WOULD SCOPE. Read from the write path itself (handle_work_ledger in crates/node/src/bin/hypervisor_daemon_routes/orchestration_routes.rs), the selection retains only entries whose project_id equals it exactly. Of 7141 ledger entries, 60 carry that field at all and 57 carry a value — and of the 542 entries that name a model, ZERO carry the key. A wired chooser would drop every invocation the estate has ever recorded and print the loss as an empty space.

AND THE ESTATE'S OWN ANSWER PROVES IT, because the page ASKS rather than re-deriving. The filter belongs to the daemon, so three principled selections are put to it on every render — the first space the plane offers, the first space value the LEDGER'S OWN rows carry that resolves to a real space, and the space key the inference lane itself writes. At port time they answered 0 entries, 34 entries (of which 0 name a model), and 0 entries. The middle one is the sharp result: a real space, present in the ledger's own vocabulary, and not one of the rows it returns is an invocation.

THE ONE PLANE THAT DOES CARRY A SPACE KEY DANGLES. The goal-run lane — 190 records fanning out into 348 declared invocation refs, the estate's real inference orchestration plane — carries a project_ref on 190 of 190. Its entire vocabulary is ONE value, and that value resolves to no record on the space plane. So the plane that could have answered 'which space ran this inference' answers with a constant that names nothing.

THREE VOCABULARIES, NO INTERSECTION. The space plane's ids, the ledger's project_id values (2 distinct, 1 resolving, 1 dangling), and the goal-run lane's project_ref (1 distinct, 0 resolving) are three different answers to what a space is. A chooser is only as real as the key it lands on, and there is no key here that all three would recognise.

AND THE EDGE IS MISSING FROM THE OTHER SIDE TOO — checked on every render rather than assumed. 0 of 11 space records carry any field naming an invocation, an inference or a model; the four ref lanes they DO carry hold 25 refs between them and 0 of those names an invocation or a model route (they hold artifact:// and receipt://project/ refs); and of the 3 published project write routes not one accepts an invocation ref — the only patch a space takes after creation is its environment-class list. On the invocation side, 0 of the 47 readable model_invocation receipts and 0 of the 10 metered usage records carry any space-, project- or tenant-named field.

AND THE VERB COULD NOT BE SPACE-SCOPED EITHER. Read from the write path (handle_model_route_invoke in crates/node/src/bin/hypervisor_daemon_routes/provider_transport.rs), the governed invoke verb accepts prompt, stream, fallback_route_refs, a retry policy, and an economics block of quote_ref + commercial_posture. Not one of the six names a space, and the record it admits carries no space field either — so a space chosen above would be dropped on submit even if a form existed to submit it.
unwritten_key_finding.why_this_is_worse_than_a_missing_route: A missing chooser is legible: the reader sees there is no way to scope and knows the estate cannot answer. A chooser wired to an unwritten key is illegible: it renders, it accepts, it filters, and it returns a confident zero that is indistinguishable from a genuinely empty space — as the first of the three asks demonstrates, since a real space with no ledger rows and a real space whose rows lack the key produce the same 0. That is REG-1's rule ('a refusal is never a zero') carried onto an AFFORDANCE: an unanswerable question rendered as an answer.

records.predicate_and_window_finding: SCH-1's rule applied to every number this surface prints. The invocation count names its predicate (a work-ledger entry whose kind is goal_run_invocation or harness_execution) and its window (the first and last timestamps among those rows, inside the ledger's own retention window, which is stated as a RETENTION window and never as a business period — no claim is made about what fell out of it). The model count names a different predicate (a non-empty implementation_result.model on the entry). The receipt count names a third (receipt.kind === 'model_invocation') with its own window and its own token sum, where an absent token field contributes nothing rather than zero. The success count is printed as what the RECORD SAYS and explicitly not as what the estate verified, because it is a self-report joined to nothing here (ING-1). And the resident-instance count is stated as a PRESENT-TENSE emptiness, never as a claim that nothing has ever been loaded.
records.named_contradiction: TWO RECEIPT FAMILIES WITH ONE NAME, and the surface refuses to adjudicate between them. The estate publishes a typed ModelInvocationReceipt readback at /v1/hypervisor/model-invocations/:id — identity-first, refused to this identity, and with NO collection route in the index at all. Beside it a different store (/v1/model-mount/receipts) answers this identity and holds 47 records whose kind is also model_invocation. Their id vocabularies differ, and the typed readback cannot be asked whether a given id exists — because refusing before the record is read is the route declining to act as an existence oracle, which is correct behaviour and is exactly what makes the join untestable here. So the surface states that the estate has not been asked, and claims neither that the families are the same nor that they are different. Preferring whichever reading suits the column header would be the surface deciding a question the estate never answered (ING-1).
records.empty_vs_missing_ruling: Three states about one screen, rendered side by side. The reference tenant's gate is EMPTY — a real chooser awaiting a pick, exactly the kind of nothing that fills. The estate's space plane is LIVE and holds 11 records. The relation between them — a space that contains an inference — is MISSING and could never fill in either direction. The port renders all three and lets none stand in for another; and it distinguishes a fourth, the invocation COLLECTION route that does not exist at all, which is not empty, not refused, and not missing-as-a-relation but simply unpublished.
